description: Matching-sampling benchmark for the Week 6 essay: structural estimators against cost-matched plain Monte Carlo on random ReLU networks.

config.model: y = a . h_L, h_l = ReLU(W_l h_{l-1} + b_l), h_0 = x; no output bias
config.context: W_l ~ N(0, sigma_w2/fan_in), b_l ~ N(0, sigma_b^2), a ~ N(0, 1/width); one draw per context
config.advice: the estimator's fixed rule; nothing depends on the context except the weights
config.common_random_numbers: contexts share standard-normal draws across sigma_w2, sigma_b and the input law
config.budget_decision: The pilot (2 pilot-stream contexts per depth, width and input law, timing only) estimated 1.25 h for the full grid with 2^21 truth pairs at width 1024. That is under the 3 h cap, so the full grid runs, and width 1024 gets 2^22 pairs (about 1.9 h).

targets.T2: P_x[y > t], t = mu_C + k sd_C, k in {3, 4}: a fixed rule applied to the C closure's own mean and standard deviation (no sampling, no truth). The same t is used to score S, D and C, so all three estimate the same number. C's estimate is then Q(k) by construction. We also record the true p at D's own threshold mu_D + k sd_D.

estimators.S: plain Monte Carlo, n = round(m * FLOPs(E) / FLOPs per sample) for E in {D, C, A4, A8} and m in {1, 10, 100}; C2 budgets match C's T2 pipeline. Independent seeds per budget and context.
estimators.D: diagonal Gaussian closure (exact univariate ReLU moments)
estimators.C: full-covariance Gaussian closure; exact bivariate ReLU moments with nonzero means (Rosenbaum 1961 truncated moments; Genz BVNU orthant probability, 20-point Gauss-Legendre in both branches); the T1 estimate uses the reduced pipeline that stops at layer L's covariance diagonal
estimators.A: conditional averaging over the first k in {4, 8} signs with the Averaging.mean_error_le budget and boundary radius exactly as boundary.py computes it, in float64; exact rationals for the validation instances (boundary.py's own code)

flop_model.sensitivity: T1_comparisons also report C and D against S matched to FLOPs with TAU = 1
flop_model.formulas: flops_forward, flops_D, flops_C, flops_A in msp.py

config.error_statistics: RMSE over contexts after subtracting the mean squared standard error of the truth (estimator and truth noise are independent); relative RMSE divides by the std of the truth across contexts with the same correction; rmse_expected for S is sqrt(mean_c Var_x(y) / n), the exact MSE of unbiased plain Monte Carlo

seeds.weights: numpy SeedSequence([base, stream, depth, width, d, context])
seeds.monte_carlo: torch CUDA generator seeded by sha256 of (msp, base, purpose, setting, context)

environment.dtype: float64 everywhere (closures, A, S and the truth)
environment.publication_note: Before publishing, the machine-specific paths in argv were rewritten to the repository-relative commands in RESULTS.md, and the hostname was removed. No measured value was changed.

univariate_relu_moments.scaling: errors divided by max(sd, |mu|) and its square

bivariate_normal_orthant.reference: Owen's T formula with scipy.special.owens_t; dblquad spot checks

bivariate_relu_moment.reference: 1D quadrature of U * E[ReLU(V) | U] (scipy quad), independent of the orthant formula

averaging_exhaustive_float64.grid: d in {8,12,16}, width in {16,64}, depth in {2,3}, sigma_w2 in {1,2,4}, sigma_b in {0,0.1}, k in {4,8} (k <= d), 4 contexts each; every one of the 2^d inputs enumerated

pilot.note: pilot-stream contexts (never used in the sweep); timing only

added_later.reason: Added after seeing the main grid: C's relative RMSE fell from width 16 to 256 but not from 256 to 1024 at input dimension 64. These settings vary the input dimension (16 and 256) at depth 2, sigma_w2 = 2, sigma_b = 0.1 to test whether that floor is set by the input dimension.
